### 3.5 Attribution — `attribution.go` + `agent.TokenAttributor`

Attribution reads the raw `full.jsonl`, not the stored compact `transcript.jsonl`: compaction drops thinking blocks and keeps only input/output tokens (no cache classes, model, or effort), so it cannot carry the cost story. It does reuse compaction's tool-detail extraction and the `ToolInvocationScanner` capability contract; `agentimport`'s per-turn splitting is reusable only at the command layer (it imports every agent package), for per-prompt grouping later — see the plan's reuse map.

Value types, capability interface, and the Claude Code implementation are as in the 08-25 spec §3.4 (`ToolUseRef`, `ToolResultRef`, `CallUsage`, `SubagentRecord`; `AttributeTokens(transcript, startLine, subagentsDir)`), with these changes:

- **Every tool-recording agent implements `TokenAttributor`**, not only Claude Code. Per-call unit and tool label: Claude `message.id` / `tool_use` blocks; Codex `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` → the next **distinct** cumulative `token_count` (delta; duplicate events ignored — Σ`last_token_usage` is ≈2× reality); OpenCode `step-start…step-finish` per assistant message / `parts[type=tool].tool`; Gemini `messages[type=gemini]` / `toolCalls[].name`; Pi `message` / `toolCall` content parts. Cursor: none.
- **Skill labels prefer the harness's own stamp.** Claude Code writes `attributionSkill` / `attributionPlugin` on each assistant line (31/40 recent checkpoints); the persisted `skill_events` anchors (`transcript_anchor{start,end,tool_use_id}`) are the second source; `tool_use name=Skill` reconstruction is the fallback for older transcripts. Labels: `Skill: <name>`; a tool call made while a skill is active is `Skill: <name> → <Tool>` so the skill's total is visible.
- **One grouping.** Rows are grouped by *what consumed the tokens* — a tool, a subagent, assistant text, context replay, the prompt/system context — and a skill that was active is an **annotation on the row** (`Bash · during systematic-debugging`), never a second row. The skill's own load cost (the Skill tool call and its result) is one row, `Skill: <name> (loaded)`. A reader adds up one column and gets the total.
- **Every cited number is visible.** A recommendation may only quote figures that appear as a row or sub-row in the tables above it — same label, same figure. Sub-rows therefore carry their share as well as tokens.
- **Drill-down inside a tool.** A tool name is not specific enough to act on; every `ToolUseRef` also carries a `Detail` taken from the tool's input so the breakdown can group one level deeper: `Bash`/`exec_command`/`bash` → the command's leading words: the first two non-flag words plus a third only if it is path-like (contains `/`, starts with `.`, or contains `*`) — `go test ./cmd/entire/...`, `git log`, `npm run`; flags, `VAR=x` prefixes, everything before the last `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`, and any word containing `://` or `@` or starting with `$` (URLs, remotes, credentials, variables) are dropped; `Read`/`read_file`/`read` → the file path; `WebFetch` → the host; `Skill` → skill name + invocation count; `Agent` (Claude Code; `Task` is legacy and never shipped)/`task`/`spawn_agent` → subagent type + the model it ran on. The `Where it went` table prints the top contributors and, indented unde
- **Rules** (agent-agnostic): a call's output → the tools it emitted (equal split, largest remainder) or `Assistant text`; a call's fresh input + cache write → the results it consumed (byte-proportional) — i.e. the *next* call pays for a tool's result; cache read → single `Context replay` row; subagent own usage (including its cache reads) → `Subagent: <type>`; same-label rows merge; sort by cost share (volume when unpriced). Invariant, tested: Σ contributors per class = flattened class totals.
- **Subagent records** for committed checkpoints come from `tasks/<tool-use-id>/task.json` via the new `SessionReader.ReadTaskRecords` (08-25 spec §3.6: required method on all six production implementers — `GitStore`, `gitRefsStore`, `kindRoutingStore`, `fanoutStore`, `fsstore.Store`, `apiCheckpointReader` — plus five test fakes; `ErrCheckpointNotFound` falls through the routing store; `(nil, nil)` when no `tasks/`). Live sessions read `agent-<id>.jsonl`.

input.prompt:
You are implementing Task 10: `tokenreport/attribution.go` — contributors (where the tokens went).

Work from the worktree at the ABSOLUTE path /Users/peytonmontei/dev/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/tokens-report (branch `tokens-report`, HEAD 30b8f122e, clean). Use absolute paths or `git -C <W>` / `go -C <W>` / `mise -C <W>` for every command — the shell cwd has been resetting to a dead directory; never rely on `pwd`. Shell is fish — quote globs. Never use `git stash` (shared stash stack) — set work aside with a WIP commit if you must.

## Goal

Turn a `*types.Attribution` (per-call usage with the tool_use blocks each call emitted and the tool results it consumed, plus subagent records) into a list of **contributors** — rows a human reads to see where tokens went: `Bash`, `Read`, `Skill: systematic-debugging (loaded)`, `Subagent: Explore`, `Assistant text`, `Context replay`, `Prompt & system context` — each with a `types.TokenUsage`, a cost share, an optional skill annotation, model, source, and up to 3 drill-down `Detail`s. Pure functions in the leaf package `tokenreport` (imports only stdlib + `cmd/entire/cli/agent/types`; it must NOT import `cmd/entire/cli`).

## Read first (all under `<W>/cmd/entire/cli/`)
- `agent/types/token_attribution.go` — the input types and every field doc (`ToolUseRef{ID,Tool,Detail,SkillName,SubagentType,Model}`, `ToolResultRef{ToolUse,Bytes}`, `CallUsage{Usage,UsageUnknown,Line,Model,Effort,At,ActiveSkill,Emitted,Consumed}`, `SubagentRecord{ToolUseID,SubagentType,Model,Usage,Start,End}`, `Attribution{Calls,Subagents,Start,End,AgentReportedCost}`). `Consumed` = tool results that are NEW input to this call, emitted by an earlier call.
- `agent/types/token_usage.go` — `TokenUsage` (7 numeric fields + Model), `AddTokenUsage` is the ONLY summing primitive (saturating, merges Model: kept when equal, "" when mixed). Use it for every sum.
- `tokenreport/cost.go` — `Weights`, `WeightsFor(model) (Weights, Family, bool)`, `WeightsForCall(model, inputTokens) Weights`, `CostShares`, `ComputeCostShares(u *types.TokenUsage, w Weights) CostShares` (`Units` = weighted cost units), `SumCostShares`. Read the docs; note `WeightsForCall` expects the input count AS THE PROVIDER COUNTS IT toward the long-context threshold (cached included) → pass `InputTokens + CacheReadTokens + CacheCreationTokens`.
- `tokenreport/format.go`, `profile.go`, `legacy.go`, `doc.go` — package style (stdlib assertions, `t.Parallel()`, doc on every exported identifier).
- `cli/attribution.go:878-910` — `largestRemainderPercent(counts []int, total int) []int` (Hamilton method, ties by lower index). You will MOVE this into `tokenreport` as exported `LargestRemainder(counts []int, total, budget int) []int` (budget parameterised: 100 for percents, `outputTokens` for splitting a call's output across N emitted tools) and make `cli/attribution.go` call `tokenreport.LargestRemainder(counts, total, 100)` — check that `cli` may import `tokenreport` (it already does for `formatTokenCount`; confirm with `grep -rn 'cli/tokenreport"' <W>/cmd/entire/cli/*.go`). Keep any existing `cli` test for it passing unchanged.
- `agent/claudecode/token_attribution.go` — the first producer, so you see real shapes (don't import it).

## Spec §3.5 rules (authoritative; also in `<W>/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-token-reports-breakdown-first-design.md` lines 118–131 — read them)
1. **Output.** A call's `OutputTokens` (and `ThinkingTokens` as a subset, split the same way) → the tools it `Emitted`, equal split with largest remainder (so Σ is exact); if it emitted nothing → the `Assistant text` contributor.
2. **Fresh input + cache write.** A call's `InputTokens`, `CacheCreationTokens` (and `CacheCreation1hTokens` subset) → the results it `Consumed`, proportional to `Bytes` (equal split when all Bytes are 0; largest remainder so Σ is exact) — i.e. the NEXT call pays for a tool's result; if it consumed nothing → the first such call's input goes to `Prompt & system context`, later calls' → `Assistant text`? NO — spec says: first call with no consumed → `Prompt & system context`; for later calls with nothing consumed, attribute fresh input + cache write to `Prompt & system context` as well (it's the user's next prompt / system re-injection). Document this.
3. **Cache read.** Every call's `CacheReadTokens` → one `Context replay` contributor.
4. **Skills.** A call with `ActiveSkill` set annotates the rows its tokens land on: tool contributors get `Skill: <ActiveSkill>` as an annotation field (NOT a second row) — so `Bash` while `systematic-debugging` is active is the contributor `{Label: "Bash", Skill: "systematic-debugging"}`, distinct from plain `{Label: "Bash"}` (merge key = Kind+Label+Skill). The `Skill` tool's own call (a ToolUseRef with `SkillName != ""`) and its result → one contributor `Skill: <name> (loaded)` (Kind skill; Label = name).
5. **Subagents.** An emitted ref with `SubagentType != ""` → contributor `Subagent: <type>` (Kind subagent, Label = type; NEVER key on the tool-name string — real Claude transcripts say `Agent`, legacy ones `Task`). It absorbs the matching `SubagentRecord`'s `Usage` (by `ToolUseID` == ref.ID) INCLUDING that record's cache reads (they are the subagent's own replay, not the parent's), and carries `Model` with precedence `record.Model` > `record.Usage.Model` > `ref.Model` (the requested alias, e.g. `haiku`). A `SubagentRecord` whose ToolUseID matches no emitted ref in the window (orphan — e.g. spawned before the window) → its own `Subagent: <type>` contributor with `Source: "task_record"`. Contributors built from calls have `Source: "transcript"`.
6. **Unresolvable results.** A `ToolResultRef` whose `ToolUse.Tool == ""` (emitted before the transcript window) → contributor `Earlier tool results` (Kind tool).
7. **Merge** same-key rows (Kind+Label+Skill) via `AddTokenUsage`; a merged row's `Model` follows AddTokenUsage's rule.
8. **Details.** Under each tool contributor, `Details` = top 3 `ToolUseRef.Detail` values (non-empty) by tokens attributed, each with `Calls` (number of refs), `Tokens` (sum of the four token classes attributed to that detail), `CostShare`. Details for `Consumed`-side attribution key on the consumed ref's `ToolUse.Detail`.
9. **Cost share.** Per call, weights = `WeightsForCall(call.Model, in+cacheRead+cacheCreate)` when `w == nil` and `WeightsFor(call.Model)` is ok; if `w != nil` use it for every call; if the model is unknown (`ok == false`) that call contributes VOLUME only — do NOT build a `CostShares` for it (a zero-Units part would clear Provider/Family in `SumCostShares`); collect such models into `Unpriced []string` on the result (deduped, order of first appearance). `Contributor.CostShare` = its cost units / total priced units (0 when nothing is priced). Sort contributors by `CostShare` desc, then by total volume desc when shares tie or nothing is priced; ties by Label asc for determinism.
10. **Invariant (tested).** For each of the 7 numeric fields: Σ over contributors == Σ over calls' `Usage` + Σ over `Subagents[].Usage`. Test it on a randomised table (seeded `math/rand/v2` with a fixed seed; ~200 iterations; random calls with random Emitted/Consumed graphs, random subagent records incl. orphans, random zero Bytes) — and also check Σ `Details[].Tokens` ≤ the contributor's volume.

## API to implement (`tokenreport/attribution.go`, tests in `attribution_test.go`)
```go
type ContributorKind string // "tool" | "skill" | "subagent" | "text" | "replay" | "prompt"
const (KindTool ContributorKind = "tool"; KindSkill = "skill"; KindSubagent = "subagent"; KindText = "text"; KindReplay = "replay"; KindPrompt = "prompt")
type Detail struct { Detail string `json:"detail"`; Calls int `json:"calls"`; Tokens int `json:"tokens"`; CostShare float64 `json:"cost_share"` }
type Contributor struct {
    Kind ContributorKind `json:"kind"`; Label string `json:"label"`; Skill string `json:"skill,omitempty"`; Model string `json:"model,omitempty"`
    Usage types.TokenUsage `json:"usage"`; CostShare float64 `json:"cost_share"`; Source string `json:"source"` // "transcript" | "task_record"
    Details []Detail `json:"details,omitempty"`
}
type Attributed struct { Contributors []Contributor `json:"contributors"`; Unpriced []string `json:"unpriced_models,omitempty"`; PricedUnits float64 `json:"priced_units"` }
func Attribute(a *types.Attribution, w *Weights) Attributed
func MergeContributors(perSession []Attributed) Attributed   // across sessions of one checkpoint: same-key merge via AddTokenUsage; CostShare recomputed over the combined PricedUnits; Unpriced union; Details re-merged and re-topped to 3
func LargestRemainder(counts []int, total, budget int) []int
```
Label constants: `LabelAssistantText = "Assistant text"`, `LabelContextReplay = "Context replay"`, `LabelPromptContext = "Prompt & system context"`, `LabelEarlierResults = "Earlier tool results"`, and for rendering `Skill: <name> (loaded)` / `Subagent: <type>` keep Label = the bare name and let the renderer prefix by Kind (document this). Display strings appear ONLY as constants here.

Nil `a` or no calls → empty `Attributed` (no panic). `UsageUnknown` calls contribute nothing but still count as a call in `Details.Calls`? — NO: a call with `UsageUnknown` has zero usage; its Emitted refs still create the contributor rows with zero tokens (so the tool appears with 0) — document and pin. Keep everything deterministic (stable sorts).

## Tests (stdlib, `t.Parallel()`), in addition to the invariant table
- output equal split across 3 emitted tools with largest remainder (e.g. 10 → 4/3/3);
- fresh input + cache write split by Bytes (12000/300) and equal when all zero;
- no-tool call → `Assistant text`; first call with nothing consumed → `Prompt & system context`; cache read → one `Context replay` row summing all calls;
- `ActiveSkill` annotation: `{Bash, Skill: systematic-debugging}` distinct from `{Bash}`; `Skill` tool call → `Skill: <name> (loaded)` row with the Skill tool's own output + its result's input;
- subagent: ref with SubagentType absorbs the matching record's Usage incl. cache reads, Model precedence all three branches; orphan record → `Source: "task_record"`;
- unresolvable result → `Earlier tool results`;
- same-key merge; sort by cost share then volume then label;
- Details: top 3 by tokens with Calls and CostShare; a 4th detail is dropped;
- cost: two calls on different models produce shares that sum to 1 across contributors (within 1e-9); an unknown-model call → listed in `Unpriced`, contributes volume, `PricedUnits` excludes it; `w != nil` overrides per-call weights; long-context tier: a `gpt-5.5` call with 200K uncached + 100K cached input lands in the 2× tier (compare against `WeightsForCall("gpt-5.5", 300_000)`);
- `MergeContributors` over two sessions merges same keys and recomputes shares;
- `LargestRemainder`: the `cli` test's expectations (find `largestRemainderPercent` tests in `cli/*_test.go` and mirror them here for budget 100) plus a budget≠100 case.

## Verify, lint, commit
- `go -C <W> build ./... && go -C <W> test -count=1 ./cmd/entire/cli/tokenreport/... ./cmd/entire/cli/` (the `cli` package is ~90–140s; run it WHOLE because you touch `cli/attribution.go`).

**Pattern kind** — the same causes, but sourced from the **profile** (recurrence across the user's recent sessions), which is what makes them general and worth remembering:

- Text: "Explore subagents ran on your main model in 31 of your last 50 sessions (about 18% of spend)." plus `Memory`: "Run Explore/search subagents on a smaller model."
- A pattern is offered by `session tokens` and `checkpoint tokens` only when the current report also exhibits the cause — so the reader sees the specific instance and the general rule together.

**Getting a pattern into the agents' instructions — one question, one write, two ways to answer:**

The write is always the same and always Entire's: append the `Memory` line under `## Token habits` in the repo instruction file(s) of the enabled agents (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md`, idempotent). Every enabled agent reads that file at session start, so the habit takes effect for all of them at once, is versioned and reviewable, and there is no per-agent memory format to know.

| who runs the report | how the question is asked | how yes is recorded |
|---|---|---|
| a human at a TTY | the report ends with `Remember for your agents? … [y/N]` (`uiform.PromptYN`) | `y` → Entire appends and marks `accepted`; `N` → `declined` |
| an agent (`--agent-brief`, no TTY) | the brief ends with the same question as text plus the exact line and file (§4.2). The agent relays it verbatim in chat. | on yes the agent makes the one-line edit itself with its own editing tools — the same edit it makes for any instruction. Entire **observes** the outcome: a pattern is `accepted` when the memory line is present in the instruction file (a read), and `declined` when it has been proposed twice with no line appearing. No flag, no command. |
| anyone, by hand | paste the `remember:` line printed in the report | same observation |

The agent never paraphrases the line — it relays a yes/no and, on yes, writes the printed line verbatim. **Why no flag and no command:** `session tokens`, `checkpoint tokens` and the `tokens` group are classified read-only in `agent-help` ("cannot change repo state"), which is what lets agents run them unprompted, so a writing flag on them is out; and no new command is wanted — the agent's own file-editing is the existing infrastructure. Entire's only agent-path involvement is reading the instruction files to see whether the line landed. The human-path `y` is an interactive write behind a TTY gate agents never reach; the classification comment notes that nuance rather than reclassifying the

const MaxRenderedRows    = 6  // top-N Contributors printed, in Attributed.Contributors order, then "(N smaller items omitted)"
const MaxRenderedDetails = 3  // rows whose Details are printed beneath them

// recommend.go
type Citation struct {
    Kind   ContributorKind `json:"kind"`             // row identity = the Kind+Label+Skill Attribute merges on
    Label  string          `json:"label"`
    Skill  string          `json:"skill,omitempty"`
    Detail string          `json:"detail,omitempty"` // Detail.Detail when a sub-row's figures are quoted; "" when only row figures are

Run/load counts now come from `selfDetail(row)` — the Detail whose `Detail == row.Label` (skill/subagent refs always carry their own name as Detail, so exactly one exists) — instead of Σ `Details.Calls`. That makes the quoted count a single visible detail's `Calls`, which the citation names. A skill row with no self-detail cannot fire repeated_skill; a subagent row without one omits "N times" and cites only the row. Both tested.

None.

1. **`tokens_profile_test.go` — the most common real-data render path has no unit test.** `tokensProfileCacheWritePart` (`tokens_profile.go:895-906`) has a `case cost.CacheWriteUnpriced` branch producing `cache write not priced (TTL not recorded)`. > **Stacked on #2155 (`tokens`).** The diff shows only this branch's commits; GitHub retargets to `main` when #2155 merges. Depends on #2155 for the `thinking_tokens` / `cache_creation_1h_tokens` / subagent `model` fields and the `token_transcript_start` window.

## Summary

Rebuilds `entire session tokens`, `entire checkpoint tokens`, and `entire tokens profile` so every report leads with **where the tokens went** — tools (with a drill-down to the command, file or host), skills, subagents, context replay, assistant text — weighted by the provider's list-price ratios per call and per model, honest about legacy checkpoints, and closed by at most two recommendations written as plain sentences whose every figure appears in a table above them. Attribution is recomputed from the agent's own transcript for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Pi; Cursor, Copilot CLI and Factory AI Droid stay totals-only and say so. Reference: `docs/architecture/token-reports.md` (written for the web team to mirror).

## What landed

- **`cmd/entire/cli/tokenreport`** — pure leaf package: price ratios per model family (verified 2026-08-28, dated in the code), per-call long-context tiers, known-TTL vs metadata pricing; attribution rules with a randomised conservation test; six calibrated recommendation causes (gates per agent from the 2026-08-28 grounding run); agent capability profiles; legacy-scope classification and dedupe; formatting.
- **`agent.TokenAttributor`** implemented by Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Pi; shared `types.TimeSpan`, `transcript.ToolDetail`/`ToolInputFromMap`/`ToolInputFromJSON`. Every attributor carries a window-independence test — which caught a real slice-boundary loss in the first two implementations before any report shipped.
- **`SessionReader.ReadTaskRecords`** across all six store implementers, so subagent rows get their type, usage and timing from the committed `tasks/<id>/task.json` records.
- **Commands** rebuilt as load → `tokenreport` → render on one shared renderer: `checkpoint tokens` (slices at `token_transcript_start`, never `checkpoint_transcript_start`; legacy checkpoints labelled and priced honestly; `--compare` gains per-class cost shares), `session tokens` (live transcript incl. subagent transcripts; `Duration: … so far`), `tokens profile` (metadata only, grouped by agent, legacy rows deduped, no recommendations in this version), bare `entire tokens` (= current session), `entire labs` row and agent-help guidance.
- **Condensation** derives `session_metrics.duration_ms` from the session's timestamps for agents that report none.
- **Fixes found on the way:** Codex counted duplicate `token_count` events as API calls (~2×) and dropped `cache_write_input_tokens`; `addCheckpointTokenUsage` silently dropped thinking and 1h cache-write tokens when flattening subagent chains (now everything sums through `types.AddTokenUsage`, saturating).

## Heads-ups for downstream consumers (entire-api / web)

- `session_metrics.duration_ms` is now present (derived) on most new checkpoints, including imported sessions.
- `checkpoint tokens --json` is additive — `context{…}` kept, `id`/`message` kept on recommendations — except `severity`/`signals` are dropped and each `contributors[]` element is now `{kind,label,skill,model,usage,cost_share,source,details[]}` (was `{tokens,percent,confidence,signals}`). New keys: `source`, `duration_seconds`, `effort`, `cost`, `legacy`, `agent_reported_cost`, `recommendations[].kind/text/cause/cited`, `comparison.cost_share`.
- `session tokens --json`: same contributor/recommendation changes; `recommendations[].id` values are now the six causes (`no-token-data`, `context-replay-hotspot`, … are gone); `contributors` is always present; a session with no recorded usage prints "Token usage: not recorded" instead of a recommendation.
- `tokens profile --json` drops `usage_scope`, `missing_token_data`, the old `tokens` object, `signals`, `recommendations`; adds `collapsed`, `excluded_test_agents`, `agents[]`, `total_tokens`.
- Codex `api_calls` now counts distinct cumulative totals; `cache_write_input_tokens` → `cache_creation_tokens`.

## Not in this PR (Plan B2)

Cross-session patterns and the `remember:` / `## Token habits` flow; `Pattern:` lines in `--agent-brief`; `Memory`/`Seen`/`Of` on recommendations stay empty. `session tokens` stays `listed: false` in agent-help until §8.7 is decided.

## Verification

- `mise run check` (fmt, lint, unit, integration): VERIFY_PLACEHOLDER
- Real-checkpoint harness (20 committed checkpoints across five agents, `checkpoint tokens --json`): provider identity exact for all 8 Gemini/OpenCode reports; legacy transcript-derived subsets match 19/19; conservation Σ contributors == totals: HARNESS_V2_PLACEHOLDER
- Every task was implemented test-first and reviewed twice (spec compliance, then code quality) before landing.

## Changelog (for release notes)

### Changed
- `entire session tokens`, `entire checkpoint tokens` and `entire tokens profile` now lead with where the tokens went — tools, skills, subagents, context replay and assistant text, with drill-down details and estimated cost shares from the provider's list-price ratios — instead of five totals and boilerplate advice. Attribution is recomputed per API call from the agent's own transcript for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Pi (Cursor, Copilot CLI and Factory AI Droid stay totals-only and say so); recommendations are at most two sentences whose every figure is visible in the tables above; legacy checkpoints are labelled and deduped rather than summed; and `session_metrics.duration_ms` is derived at condensation for agents that report none ([#2165](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2165))

### Fixed
- Codex API-call counts no longer double-count duplicate `token_count` events, and `cache_write_input_tokens` is recorded ([#2165](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2165))

Yes — trail 1167 is PR #2155 (`tokens`, PR A). Findings don't live on the trail sub-endpoints (404); they're Cursor Bugbot review threads on the PR. There are **3 unresolved, all Medium, all anchored at commit `6c6225807`**. I verified each against the code rather than taking the bot's word — all three are real.

**Trail monitors:** Security 8 (▼7), Risk 35 (▼10), Drift 6 (▼4), Confidence 78 (—). Status open, phase building.

---

### 1. Token window advanced past uncounted tail at turn end — `manual_commit_hooks.go:2940` ✅ real

After a mid-turn commit, `HandleTurnEnd` calls `advanceTranscriptWindows(state, pos)`, which sets **both** `CheckpointTranscriptStart` and `TokenTranscriptStart` to the turn-end offset. But the checkpoint that was condensed at commit time measured its `token_usage` only up to the commit-time transcript end, and I confirmed `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` (`:3021`) rewrites **only the transcript** — it issues `checkpoint.SessionTranscript(updateOpts)` with no token recompute. So the tail (`[commit-time end, turn end)` — final assistant messages, their `token_count` events, tool results) is in no checkpoint's delta, and the next checkpoint starts after it. Those tokens are dropped permanently.

The comment right there justifies the advance for the *transcript* (avoid re-including condensed content) — correct for transcripts, wrong for tokens. Carry-forward already makes exactly this distinction at `:3338` ("TokenTranscriptStart is deliberately NOT reset").

**Fix shape:** one line — set `state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = pos` directly instead of calling `advanceTranscriptWindows`. No double-count risk, since the tail is currently counted nowhere.

### 2. Session total overwritten with a checkpoint delta — `manual_commit_condensation.go:1173` ✅ real (PR A regression)

`applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` (called at `:561` with `sessionData.TokenUsage`) ends in `state.TokenUsage = withSubagentTokensFrom(backfillUsage, …)`. For every non-Copilot agent, `sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage` falls through to `return checkpointUsage` — which **after PR A is the per-checkpoint delta**. Meanwhile `state.TokenUsage` is the session cumulative, accumulated across steps at `manual_commit_git.go:125`, and `entire status` reads it as the session total (`status.go:594`).

So from the second condensation onward, `entire status` reports "latest checkpoint delta + steps since" instead of the session total. This was harmless before PR A (the checkpoint value was cumulative-from-0); the rescoping is what broke it. The Copilot branch is fine — it recomputes from offset 0.

**Fix shape:** only adopt the backfill when it's genuinely session-wide (the Copilot full-transcript branch); otherwise leave `state.TokenUsage` alone. The two later `return checkpointUsage` branches are the offenders.

### 3. `token_usage_version: 2` stamped onto legacy checkpoints — `persistent.go:829` / `fsstore.go:147` ✅ real, narrow

Both writers set `TokenUsageVersion: TokenUsageVersionDelta` unconditionally on every root-metadata rewrite — no preservation of an existing lower value, unlike the sibling fields (`commitSHA`, `hasReview`, `imported`) that are deliberately carried forward from `existingSummary` a few lines above. Any pre-upgrade checkpoint that gets a later write (the code's own example: a review session attached to it) is promoted to 2 while its existing session rows still hold legacy cumulative totals.

That matters because the reader keys off it: `tokenreport.ClassifyScope` returns `ScopeDelta` for `Version >= 2` and skips `DedupeLegacyCheckpoints` — so PR B's `tokens profile` would sum rows that are running totals. Narrow (needs an old checkpoint rewritten by a new CLI) but silently wrong when it hits.

**Fix shape:** hoist an `existingVersion` out of the `if entry, exists` block and keep the lower value on rewrite; only stamp 2 when there's no existing summary (or it's already 2). Same in `fsstore.go`.

---

**Where this leaves us:** all three are in PR A's write side, so fixes land on `tokens` — which means rebasing #2165 on top (61 commits, mechanical but not free). #1 and #2 I'd call worth fixing before merge: both silently undercount, and #2 is a user-visible `entire status` regression this PR introduced. #3 is defensible as a follow-up if you'd rather not touch the stack again, though it's the smallest of the three.

Your call on whether I fix all three on `tokens` now, fix #1+#2 and file #3, or leave them and reply on the threads. I haven't touched any code.

content.text:
My mistake — I gave you the GitHub Bugbot threads. Here are the actual trail findings: **6 from Soph, all open, all marked `current` (not stale)**, on code version `01M15F9YFH…`. Two of them Bugbot never found, and Soph's read on the shared ones is sharper. I verified all six against the code.

### HIGH — tokens in the post-commit tail are recorded in no checkpoint
`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:2940` (conf 0.90)

After a complete mid-turn commit, condensation writes the checkpoint over `[TokenStart, N]` and sets both offsets to N. `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` then rewrites that checkpoint with `SessionTranscript(updateOpts)` only — transcript, assets, prompts, skill events, **no token recompute**. This line then advances the token window to M, so `(N, M]` lands nowhere. That tail is exactly where the tokens are: the site's own comment names "tool results, token counts, task_complete", and for Codex the whole turn's accounting arrives after the commit.

**Confirmed** — I traced `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` (`:3021`) and it writes transcript only. Soph's fix is right and minimal: set only `CheckpointTranscriptStart`, the same divergence the PR already makes for carry-forward. Also flags that the new integration test covers carry-forward, not this path.

### MEDIUM — `state.TokenUsage` overwritten with a per-checkpoint delta
`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1173` (conf 0.85)

`state.TokenUsage` is the session accumulator (`manual_commit_git.go:125`) that `entire status` reads; `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` overwrites it with `checkpointUsage`, which after this PR is always a delta.

**Confirmed**, and Soph adds what I got wrong: the clobber isn't new — the `:1191` fallback predates the PR (`9f8ef976e`). What PR A removed is the accidental repair (post-carry-forward condensations used to recompute from offset 0 and restore a cumulative value). So it's a pre-existing bug the PR stops masking. Their consequence point: **the PR description's "No output changes" claim isn't true** — `entire status`' session total changes in the carry-forward case. Fix the backfill or drop the claim.

### MEDIUM — load-bearing doc comment reattached to the wrong function
`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_git.go:496` (conf 0.95)

`advanceTranscriptWindows` was inserted between `resetCheckpointWindow` and its doc comment. **Confirmed by reading 486–512**: the block covering `SubagentTokensBaseline` rescoping and the #2058 task-record contract ("the single post-write mutation site") now renders as `advanceTranscriptWindows`' godoc, and `resetCheckpointWindow` at `:509` has no comment at all. Mechanical slip, trivially fixed by moving the new function below.

### LOW — `token_usage_version: 2` asserted over legacy sessions
`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:829` (conf 0.60)

Stamped unconditionally even when a session is added to an existing summary (`:620` copies `existingSummary.Sessions`), so a CLI upgrade between two writes to one checkpoint asserts v2 over sessions whose `token_usage` is still legacy-cumulative — and readers then skip per-session dedupe. Soph rates the window narrow and points at the durable issue underneath: **`token_usage_version` is a summary-level flag for a per-session property.** Confirmed (no preservation of an existing value, unlike the sibling `commitSHA`/`hasReview`/`imported` carry-forwards right above it).

### LOW — OpenCode thinking tokens can exceed output tokens
`cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/transcript.go:305` (conf 0.70)

`BilledOutput()` (`types.go:87`) only folds `Reasoning` in when `Total` reconciles exactly; line 305 adds `Reasoning` to `ThinkingTokens` unconditionally. If a version omits `total` and reasoning sits outside output, `ThinkingTokens > OutputTokens`, violating the subset contract the docs promise — a reader computing non-thinking output gets a negative. Soph notes the fallback assumes the *less* common shape (7,456 messages with reasoning outside output vs 2,991 inside) but verified `total` present on all 116 committed transcripts: **hardening, not a live bug**. Fix = explicit `Total == 0` branch or clamp against `BilledOutput`.

### LOW — doc says `token_transcript_start` presence marks v2
`api/checkpoint/metadata.go:437` (conf 0.90)

With `omitempty` the field also drops at offset 0, so a session's *first* v2 checkpoint omits it. Behaviourally harmless (readers default to 0, correct there) but presence isn't a v2 marker, and both the field comment and `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` read as if it were. Confirmed verbatim in the field doc.

---

**Overlap with what I showed you before:** Bugbot's three are a subset — the HIGH one, the `state.TokenUsage` one, and the version stamp. Soph additionally caught the godoc slip, the OpenCode subset-contract gap, and the doc nit, and correctly identified that the `state.TokenUsage` clobber predates this PR.

One loose end: the trail reports `unresolvedCount: 8` against 6 findings and 0 trail comments — I couldn't account for the other 2 from the API, so there may be items on an earlier code version that this endpoint doesn't return.

My read on priority: the HIGH is a genuine silent token loss and should land before merge; the godoc slip and the two docs/hardening LOWs are cheap enough to fold into the same pass; the `state.TokenUsage` one needs a decision from you — fix it here (it's not this PR's bug, but this PR is what unmasks it) or drop the "No output changes" line from the PR body and file it. Fixes land on `tokens`, so #2165 needs a rebase after. Nothing touched yet — say the word on which set.

yes so please fix these, be careful about the fixes so that you're carefully approaching the fix as to not introduce unintended behavior after the fix and so we dont introduce high risk or secuirty or more findings. Also, see these findings after we thought this trail was ready

Right — and that's the real lesson here: I called #2155 ready without ever checking the trail's own review findings. I'll fix all six, carefully, and I'll verify each fix can't shift behavior elsewhere before I touch anything.

Starting with the highest-risk one: the token/transcript offsets can only safely diverge if the slicing code doesn't assume they're equal.

// TestHandleTurnEnd_MidTurnCommit_KeepsTokenWindow locks the offset split at
// the turn-end advance after a complete mid-turn commit.
//
// Condensation writes the checkpoint's token_usage over
// [TokenTranscriptStart, N] and finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints then rewrites that
// checkpoint with the full transcript only — no token recompute. If the turn-end
// advance moved BOTH offsets to the turn's end M, the tokens recorded in
// (N, M] (tool results, token counts, task_complete — for Codex the turn's whole
// accounting) would belong to no checkpoint: the finalized one measured up to N,
// and the next one starts after M. Only the stored-transcript offset may move.
func TestHandleTurnEnd_MidTurnCommit_KeepsTokenWindow(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = repo.Close() })

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "test-turn-end-token-window"

	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)

	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	state.Phase = session.PhaseActive
	state.AgentType = agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

	// Mid-turn commit: condensation advances both offsets to the transcript
	// end as it stood at commit time.
	commitWithCheckpointTrailer(t, repo, dir, "a1b2c3d4e5f6")
	require.NoError(t, s.PostCommit(context.Background()))

	state, err = s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotEmpty(t, state.TurnCheckpointIDs,
		"mid-turn commit should leave a checkpoint to finalize at turn end")
	require.Empty(t, state.FilesTouched,
		"a complete mid-turn commit leaves no uncommitted work (the carry-forward guard)")
	tokenStartAtCommit := state.TokenTranscriptStart
	require.Positive(t, tokenStartAtCommit,
		"condensation should have advanced the token window past the condensed content")

	// The agent keeps writing after the commit: this tail carries the turn's
	// remaining token accounting and was never condensed.
	tailTranscript := testTranscriptPromptResponse +
		`{"type":"human","message":{"content":"and now the tail"}}` + "\n" +
		`{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":"tail response"}}` + "\n"
	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(dir, ".entire", "metadata", sessionID, "full_transcript.jsonl")
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(transcriptPath), 0o755))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(transcriptPath, []byte(tailTranscript), 0o644))
	state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

	require.NoError(t, s.HandleTurnEnd(context.Background(), state))

	assert.Greater(t, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart, tokenStartAtCommit,
		"the stored-transcript offset must advance to the turn end so the next "+
			"checkpoint's transcript does not re-include condensed content")
	assert.Equal(t, tokenStartAtCommit, state.TokenTranscriptStart,
		"the token window must stay where condensation left it: the tail's tokens "+
			"were not counted into the finalized checkpoint, so they belong to the next one")
}
EOF

Fix token counting and persist what agents record (thinking, cache TTL, subagent model, token_usage_version)
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1167
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Write-side fixes for the token data behind `session tokens`, `checkpoint tokens`, and `tokens profile`. **No output changes** — this PR makes the numbers written into checkpoints correct and complete; the report redesign follows in a separate PR off main.

Five commits, each independently reviewable:

### 1. `fix(tokens)`: Gemini and OpenCode parsers
- **Gemini** counted `cached` twice (it is a subset of `input`) and dropped `thoughts` (reported outside `output`). Real committed checkpoints were inflated 58–89%, with output understated 34–47%. Fresh input is now `input − cached + tool`; output is `output + thoughts`.
- **OpenCode** ignored `reasoning`, which is outside `output` in some versions and inside in others (7,456 vs 2,991 assistant messages in this repo's history). `Tokens.BilledOutput()` uses the per-message `total` identity to count it exactly once.
- Verified against every committed Gemini (19/19) and OpenCode (116/116) transcript on `entire/checkpoints/v1`: the four classes now sum to the provider's own total on all of them.

### 2. `fix(strategy)`: checkpoint `token_usage` gets its own window
`carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart` to 0 after a partial commit (deliberately, for a self-contained transcript). Checkpoint tokens were computed from the same offset, so every post-carry-forward checkpoint re-reported the **whole session's** tokens: 53% of non-first checkpoints in this repo's history, 65% of all cache-read tokens ever recorded are re-counts, and anything summing `token_usage` was inflated 2–3×. `SessionState.TokenTranscriptStart` now scopes tokens; `advanceTranscriptWindows` moves both offsets at every condensation site; carry-forward resets only the transcript one. Legacy state files migrate on load.

### 3. `feat(tokens)`: persist what the agents already record
- `types.TokenUsage` gains `thinking_tokens` (⊂ `output_tokens`) and `cache_creation_1h_tokens` (⊂ `cache_creation_tokens`), both `omitempty`, **read verbatim from agent fields, never inferred** — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini for thinking; Claude Code and Pi for the 1-hour cache TTL (priced 2× vs 1.25×; sessions are usually all-one-or-the-other). Plus `model` on subagent entries so cost can be weighted per model.
- `AddTokenUsage` / `SubtractTokenUsage` / `accumulateTokenUsage` carry the new fields at every nesting level; Claude's subagent aggregation goes through `AddTokenUsage` instead of a field-by-field loop.
- Root `metadata.json` stamps `token_usage_version: 2`. Absent = legacy checkpoint whose `token_usage` may be a session-cumulative total.

### 4. `feat(checkpoint)`: persist `token_transcript_start`
Each session's `metadata.json` now records where its token window began. Without it a reader attributing a checkpoint's tokens from the stored `full.jsonl` had nothing to slice at — `checkpoint_transcript_start` is reset to 0 by carry-forward, so slicing there would re-create the cumulative bug. Present on `token_usage_version ≥ 2` checkpoints, absent on legacy ones.

## For the web team
`docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` → "`token_usage` contract": field semantics, the subset rule (four-class sum unchanged), **absence is "not recorded", not zero**, the legacy dedupe rule (per session: latest cumulative snapshot + later deltas), never pricing an unknown cache TTL, per-model weighting, and don't key on `cli_version` (it's `"dev"` on most rows). Additive only — no existing reader breaks. Metadata grows ~24 B per checkpoint and ~58 B on Claude session entries.

## Behaviour changes to note in the changelog
- New Gemini checkpoints record smaller totals (no double-counted cache) and larger output (thoughts included); new OpenCode checkpoints record larger output (reasoning included).
- New checkpoints after a partial commit record only that checkpoint's tokens, not the session's running total.

## Test plan
- Every change was test-first; tests whose RED was compile-blocked were mutation-checked afterwards (each fails when its production line is removed).
- New: Gemini/OpenCode identity tests, `TestCondenseSession_TokenWindowSurvivesCarryForward` (+ end-to-end assertion in the PostCommit carry-forward test), subset-field tests for all five parsers, `AddTokenUsage`/`accumulateTokenUsage` subset + model tests, `TestGitStore_Write_StampsTokenUsageVersion`.
- Seven existing tests that had the double count baked into expected values were corrected.
- New end-to-end integration test `TestTokenWindow_SurvivesCarryForwardEndToEnd` drives the partial-commit carry-forward through the real hooks and asserts the committed `token_transcript_start` and `token_usage_version` (mutation-checked: re-adding the token-window reset fails it) — added for the coverage gap the Entire confidence monitor flagged.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`: 0 issues. `mise run test:integration`: pass. `mise run test`: pass (locally only `redact.TestBetterleaksDoesNotPoisonGitEnvironment` fails — it writes an unquoted `replace => <repoRoot>` and this machine's path has spaces; unrelated, passes in CI).
- Real-data verification of the fixed parsers on 135 committed checkpoints as above.

> Checkpoint **`token_usage`** is now a true per-checkpoint delta instead of re-reporting session totals after partial-commit carry-forward. **`SessionState.TokenTranscriptStart`** scopes token recomputation separately from **`CheckpointTranscriptStart`**; **`advanceTranscriptWindows`** updates both at condensation, while carry-forward still resets only the transcript offset. All six fixes are in and the diff is lint-clean. Two verifications are running in the background: the full CI suite (`caffeinate -i -s mise run test:ci`) and an independent adversarial review of the diff. I'll report both when they land.

Summary of what changed, one fix per finding:

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| HIGH — post-commit tail counted nowhere | `manual_commit_hooks.go` turn-end advance now calls the new `advanceStoredTranscriptWindow` (transcript offset only); token window stays where condensation left it |
| MED — session total clobbered | `sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage` now returns `sessionWide`; only a session-wide recompute may replace `state.TokenUsage`, delta stays a last-resort fill |

| LOW — v2 stamped over legacy rows | new shared `ResolveTokenUsageVersion` policy, used by both the git store and fsstore |
| LOW — thinking > output | OpenCode reasoning capped at the output actually billed |
| LOW — doc claims presence marks v2 | corrected in the field comment and `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` |

Two things worth flagging now:

- **Each behavioral fix was verified red-then-green.** For the HIGH one I temporarily reverted the call site to confirm the new test actually fails against the old behavior (it does, on the exact assertion), then restored it. My own table-test also caught an over-reach in my first version of the version policy — it downgraded a hypothetical future version — so the rule is now "report the weakest guarantee across rows."

The turn-end site was genuinely the only one that should diverge, matching the reviewer's read.

On your last point — that's on me. I flipped #2155 to ready without ever reading the trail's own findings, and then when you asked I handed you Cursor's GitHub threads instead of Soph's. I've written that into memory as a hard step: pull `/api/v1/trails/gh/<owner>/<repo>/<n>/reviews/comments` **before** calling a PR ready, and treat trail findings as a separate source from GitHub review threads.
